*   **Limitations:** Point-sampling of slices may introduce staircase artifacts compared to pre-integrated slab methods; requires careful handling of pre-integration due to warping-induced non-orthogonality [S1].

The claim states that point-sampling of slices may introduce staircase artifacts compared to pre-integrated slab methods and requires careful handling of pre-integration due to warping-induced non-orthogonality. Source [S1] explicitly supports both parts of this claim: 1) It states that the method extracts kernel slices (point-sampling) unlike the previous slab method which pre-filters, and notes that 'To overcome possible staircase artifacts... one could easily add pre-integrated rendering'. 2) It explains that 'warping undoes the orthogonality of the rays' and that storing pre-integrated slab integrals leads to errors because 'The integrals for warped rays would be looked up incorrectly', thus requiring careful handling (specifically, not storing slab integrals but using a cross-sectional texture instead).
